feedback.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(y)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(1<Y<\frac{5}{2}).$

| $y$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{3}{2}$ | $2$ | $\frac{5}{2}$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(y)$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.6$ | $0.7$ | $0.8$ | $1.0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is a function $F(y)$ such that

$$
F(y)=P(Y\le y).
$$

To compute the probability of a random variable $Y$ over an interval, we can use the rule

$$
P(a<Y\le b)=F(b)-F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P(1<Y<\frac{5}{2}).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $a<Y<b,$ not $a<Y\le b.$

So first, we must convert the interval $1<Y<\frac{5}{2}$ to the form $a<Y\le b.$ Looking at the given possible values of $Y,$ we see that $Y<\frac{5}{2}$ is equivalent to $Y\le 2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<Y<\frac{5}{2}) & =P(1<Y\le 2) \\  & =F(2)-F(1) \\  & =0.7-0.3 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
